name.en: Fake traffic fine text in the name of the Belize Police

how.en: A text message or online notice says you committed a traffic offence and must pay a fine on a website. It threatens to suspend your licence or take legal action if you do not pay. The Belize Police Department says it did not send it: the website copies an official government page to take your money and card or personal details.

text.en: A text or online notice claims to come from the Belize Police Department about a traffic offence.
It warns that your licence will be suspended or you will face legal action unless you pay.
It sends you to a website that looks like an official government page.
You are asked to pay the fine and enter card or personal details there.
The money and details go to the criminals.

BELIZE POLICE DEPT: Notice of traffic violation - vehicle recorded exceeding speed limit on George Price Hwy. Fine BZ$75 must be settled within 48hrs or your drivers licence will be suspended. Pay online: [link]

en: text saying i have a traffic fine from belize police
pay traffic ticket online link text
police traffic violation notice by text message
drivers licence will be suspended unless i pay the fine
unpaid traffic fine sms with a link
A traffic fine arrives by text with a link to pay online.
It threatens licence suspension or court action to rush you.
The website asks for card details or personal information.
Don’t click the link and don’t pay.
Check any traffic notice through official Government of Belize channels or at a police station.
If you entered card details, call your bank to block the card.
Report the message to the police.
